description: Reusable authored-pose direction for berserker player identities. Registry metadata and the staged portrait control identity; this profile supplies ferocious dual-weapon choreography and continuity rules.

style.authority: Pixel density, outline language, compact tactical proportions, lighting, and material rendering only. The style image must never override the selected identity portrait or player metadata.

identity.motionStyle: ferocious, explosive, top-heavy, and relentless, with deep planted lunges, broad shoulder rotation, and readable dual-weapon momentum
identity.equipmentRule: Preserve the portrait's savage armor, war paint, scars, hair, and exact weapon designs and count. If two axes are present, keep exactly one in each original hand; never duplicate, swap, sheath, merge, or transform them.
identity.magicRule: Berserker power is physical fury. Use no spells, runes, projectiles, elemental trails, or supernatural aura; restrained dust or a short impact slash may follow physical contact only.

promptTemplates.reference: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: canonical full-body game character reference for a 16-bit fantasy tactical RPG. Image 1 is the authoritative {{displayName}} identity portrait; Image 2 is the approved full-body pixel-art style and proportion reference only. Player identity metadata: {{visualTraits}}. Create one complete head-to-toe {{displayName}} preserving Image 1's face, ancestry traits, gender presentation, hair, scars, war paint, savage armor, palette, proportions, and weapons. Do not import identity details from Image 2. {{equipmentRule}} Translate the portrait into a compact powerful full-body silhouette. Use a {{background}} background with no floor or scenery and a square 1:1 canvas with generous padding. Polished hand-authored 16-bit pixel art with crisp pixel clusters, bold dark outlines, restrained warm top-left highlights, and muted watercolor-and-parchment ramps. One centered berserker in a coiled aggressive guard facing {{baseFacing}}. {{invariants}}
promptTemplates.animation: Draw exactly {{frameCount}} genuinely redrawn full-body {{actionLabel}} poses of the authoritative {{displayName}} in a {{columns}}-column by {{rows}}-row atlas, ordered top row left-to-right then bottom row left-to-right. Player identity metadata: {{visualTraits}}. Required sequence: {{frameSequence}}. Motion direction: {{motionDirection}}. Overall berserker motion is {{motionStyle}}. {{poseRequirement}} Preserve exact identity, armor, palette, proportions, scars, war paint, and weapon count. {{equipmentRule}} {{magicRule}} Action-specific effects: {{effectRule}} Use a {{background}} background with generous gutters between complete head-to-toe poses. {{invariants}}

idle.motionDirection: A predatory breathing loop shifts weight between a low weapon guard and an impatient forward lean while both weapons remain controlled.
idle.effectRule: No active attack effect; hair, straps, and weapon heads may settle with the heavy breathing.
frameDescriptions: low aggressive guard with both weapons spread
deep inhale lifting shoulders and weapon heads
weight drives onto the forward foot
impatient forward lean with elbows flexed
centered predatory crouch
forceful exhale lowering shoulders
rearward weight shift with weapons re-angled
coiled guard flowing back to frame one

walk.motionDirection: A fast heavy-footed stalk uses alternating contacts, deep compression, broad counter-swings, and controlled weapon inertia.
walk.effectRule: No attack trail or magic; armor, hair, straps, and weapons follow the planted steps.
frameDescriptions: left foot crushing forward contact
left leg compressed under the weapon weight
passing pose with right knee driving through
right foot reaching as both weapons counter-swing
right foot forceful forward contact
right leg compressed under the armor
passing pose with left knee driving through
left foot reaching into the stalking loop

attack.motionDirection: A committed combination coils both weapons, drives a first diagonal chop, crosses into a second strike, follows through low, and recovers into guard.
attack.effectRule: Two short physical blade-swish accents may mark the separate contacts; no projectile, magic, duplicate weapon, or effect hiding the arms.
frameDescriptions: coiled dual-weapon guard
rear weapon pulls high as the lead weapon measures distance
deep crossed windup over the rear leg
lunging first diagonal chop with hips committed
second weapon crosses through the contact line
low full-body follow-through with both arms separated
weapons recoil outward while feet reset
recovered aggressive guard

hurt.motionDirection: A hard hit breaks the attack posture into an articulated recoil, staggering step, low weapon brace, furious rise, and renewed guard.
hurt.effectRule: One compact physical impact accent only; no blood, gore, tint, magic, or dropped or duplicated weapon.
frameDescriptions: aggressive guard before impact
sharp torso flinch with both grips retained
maximum backward twist and knee collapse
staggering rear step with weapons spread for balance
low crossed-weapon brace
furious push upright through bent legs
feet reset as weapons rise
recovered enraged guard

death.motionDirection: A final impact empties the fury, weapons sink, knees buckle, the body turns into a grounded side collapse, and all motion settles into a fully fallen pose.
death.effectRule: No gore, blood, magic, or rigid rotation. Keep every weapon single and recognizable through the articulated fall.

weapon arms sag as balance fails
both knees buckle beneath the armor
one hip grounds while the torso twists sideways
body and weapons descend into full ground contact
low fallen body settles with limbs articulated
final fully fallen berserker with weapons at rest
same final fallen pose held

victory.motionDirection: The berserker recognizes victory, stamps forward, sweeps both weapons wide, throws the chest upward in a roar, crosses the weapons overhead, and holds a dominant finish.
victory.effectRule: No spell effect; a tiny metal glint and grounded dust at the stamp may accent the physical celebration.
